headline: Thailand Plans Chemical Export Halt for Myanmar Rare-Earth Mining
deck: Officials describe a proposed export and transit ban as ministries review rules; China and Myanmar talks are scheduled for Monday.
body: Thailand is preparing to ban the export and transit of chemicals used in rare-earth mining and processing; Reuters reported that the country plans to stop exports of chemicals used in Myanmar’s rare-earth mining. The Nation said the proposed controls are part of a campaign against toxic contamination in northern rivers. [E1][E2]

Yodchanan said the government would pursue restrictions on the export and transit of precursor chemicals associated with rare-earth mining and processing through National Security Council mechanisms. The Industry and Commerce ministries will review relevant regulations to establish controls while minimizing unintended consequences for legitimate businesses. [E3][E4]

Thailand has coordinated with China and Myanmar to prepare a ministerial-level meeting on 24 November, Thairath reported. Payu said one domestic measure would use the National Security Council mechanism to immediately ban exports of rare-earth mining precursor chemicals to Myanmar. [E5][E6]
